features.name: New companion table schema for table extensions
features.description: Changed the data model from storing each table extension in its own table to having one companion table that stores all extension fields, reducing the number of database joins from n to 1.
caveats: Performance gains vary based on number of extensions and code organization
Only visible benefit with 2 or more extensions
Requires upgrade work for on-premises installations

features.name: Delete operation performance improvement
features.description: Delete operations are now 2 to 5 times faster with the new companion table model.
caveats: Actual performance gains depend on code and data configuration

features.name: Insert operation performance improvement
features.description: Insert performance is approximately twice as fast with the new model.
caveats: Performance depends on event handling and code organization

features.name: Modify operation performance improvement
features.description: Modify operations can be up to 2 times faster with the new schema.
caveats: Performance gains less dramatic than reads due to event invocation

features.name: Read operation performance improvement
features.description: Read performance shows the most significant improvement, with nearly flat scaling as the number of table extensions increases, compared to the previous linear scaling.
caveats: Performance measurement requires flushing server caches
Actual gains depend on field count and data page usage

features.name: Database size reduction from new schema
features.description: The new companion table model decreases overall database size because there is only one copy of the primary key, row version, and other metadata instead of duplicates across multiple extension tables.

features.name: Cloud migration support for new schema
features.description: Version 23 includes full cloud migration support from earlier versions to the new schema. The cloud migration tool was updated to work as a data factory and understands both the old and new data models.

features.name: Database views for on-premises ETL tools
features.description: To support on-premises installations that have direct database integrations with ETL or BI tools, the new schema can be mimicked using database views so existing queries continue to work without changes.
caveats: Direct database access is not officially supported
Code samples are available on GitHub

features.name: SetLoadFields continuing value with new schema
features.description: SetLoadFields remains useful even with the new schema because it limits the fields loaded into memory, reducing data transfer and caching overhead, and can help hit covering indexes for performance-critical loops.
caveats: Less critical for general code paths that were not previously optimized

features.name: Set-based load fields method for base table owners
features.description: A new method was introduced that allows owners of base tables to set loading of all base fields at once, reducing code maintenance and still providing performance benefits.
caveats: Example shown on VAT Entry table
Still requires careful consideration for truly performance-critical code

features.name: Orphaned Extension Data Cleanup
features.description: Added ability to delete orphaned extension data left behind after uninstalling extensions, now impacting performance as data is part of extension table rows. Tool placed in installed extensions section.
caveats: Orphaned data now impacts database capacity and join performance
Reinstalling extension after cleanup will not restore deleted data

features.name: New Locking Model
features.description: Changed locking behavior to use read committed instead of update lock for new record instances on modified tables, reducing inadvertent locking of other records and enabling more concurrent access.
caveats: Existing tenants must opt-in via feature management
Environment restart required to apply switch
May expose different concurrency issues in certain code paths
Lock table statement still available if explicit locking needed

features.name: Read Isolation Property
features.description: AL property allowing control of locking behavior on instance level, enabling opt-out from automatic update locks without using lock table statement.
caveats: Requires explicit property configuration on record instances

features.name: AutoIncrement Field Performance Optimization
features.description: Fixed optimization for autoincrement fields that made wide tables slow due to inefficient parameter generation algorithm, now significantly faster even with 100 fields.
caveats: Was causing seconds of delay with 100 autoincrement fields

features.name: Set Range SQL Query Optimization
features.description: Optimized SQL queries generated from set range to better enable index selection by SQL optimizer.

features.name: Removal of Force Order and Loop Joints Server Settings
features.description: Server settings for Force Order and Loop Joints will be removed in 2024 release wave one to standardize query execution approach.
features.status_evidence_quote: upcoming in 2024 release way one the server settings for Force order and loop joints will be removed
caveats: Coming in next release

features.name: Removal of App Database Write Capability
features.description: On-premises ability to write to the app database will be removed in next release, eliminating app database as a concept.
caveats: Six months notice before enforcement
